text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000373 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation across every complexity band, but the records review is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. About a third of 99215s fall on low-complexity patients, and the low-complexity sample includes routine-looking diagnoses such as Z09 follow-ups, M54.50 low back pain and J06.9 upper respiratory infection (e.g., C0186381, C0186772, C0187375). That pattern is more consistent with upcoding than with a sicker panel. Against this, the documentation is thin: only 9 documented 99215 claims, with 2 below the billed level (C0186620, C0187083) and several supported at high MDM (C0186359, C0186867, C0187407), so the unsupported rate sits between the rule's cutoffs and cannot settle the question. The note signals are modest: the problem flags are worth a look (C0187083 also appears among the below-billed claims), and there are a few no-lab notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed, which is weak evidence at most, while the missing audit trail leaves cloning or bulk creation untested. A reviewer should first request more charts, prioritizing 99215 claims on 0–1 condition patients from the low-complexity sample, along with the audit trail, to see whether the documented MDM actually supports the billed level."}
